assumptions: Assay compatibility controls (capture-reagent buffer panels) will detect and exclude direct assay interference by formulation or matrix components.
The exogenous intact-EV spike-in is analytically distinguishable from endogenous EVs to permit within-sample recovery control.
The selected in vitro neuroinflammation assay is sensitive and specific enough to detect relevant modulation from fraction eluates.
biological_rationale: Rodent intranasal efficacy reports support a secretome/EV-driven bioactivity signal but do not link activity to intact, membrane-protected EVs. MISEV2023 recommends orthogonal, membrane-protection controls and spike-ins to exclude assay failures or non-vesicular co-isolates. A spike-in-controlled, fraction-level functional assay directly links an intact-EV-associated signature to measurable bioactivity and discriminates EV-dependent versus soluble-secretome-driven effects prior to manufacturing commitments.

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Qualitative pass/fail: bounded fraction = EV-enriched if spike-in recovery + endogenous capture co-localization + detergent/protease-sensitive bioactivity observed.
candidate_quality_attributes.name: EV identity and purity
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: This experiment operationalizes an orthogonal identity gate (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease sensitivity) and pairs it with spike-in recovery to control assay performance; it feeds directly into defining EV identity and purity for SGL-001.
candidate_quality_attributes.uncertainty: Moderate: success depends on capture reagent performance and functional assay sensitivity.

edges.competing_explanation: Observed in vitro bioactivity could result from soluble proteins or non-vesicular co-isolates that co-fractionate, rather than EV-associated cargo.
edges.missing_experiment: Fraction-level spike-in-controlled functional co-fractionation with detergent/protease protection controls.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: literature and consensus guidance recommend membrane-protection and orthogonal assays but do not provide program-specific linkage to the selected in vitro readout.

edges.competing_explanation: Failure to detect intact-EV exposure in vivo may arise from administration, labeling sensitivity, or species clearance differences rather than absence of EV-associated cargo.
edges.missing_experiment: Short-interval in vivo/bridging verification using materials classified by the proposed spike-in-controlled identity assay.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate-to-high: large-animal negative biodistribution increases the operational importance of proving intact-EV identity and excluding assay failure, but species- and administration-related factors remain competing explanations.

nodes.statement: An orthogonal intact-EV signature (exogenous spike-in recovery + endogenous capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease sensitivity) identifies a membrane-protected particle fraction distinct from non-vesicular secretome co-isolates.

If the membrane-protected particle fraction contains a reproducible neuroinflammation-modulating bioactivity in vitro that is abolished by detergent/protease treatment, then the bioactivity is plausibly EV-associated rather than driven by soluble secretome co-isolates.

If the secretome-retaining concentrated conditioned medium lacks spike-in-validated, capture-positive particle co-localization or contains detergent-insensitive activity, then the functional signal is likely non-EV and the material should be treated as secretome for product-definition and CMC planning.

competing_explanations: Functional signals could be mediated by soluble secretome components that co-elute with particles in the chosen fractionation window.
Apparent detergent/protease sensitivity might reflect loss of an assay-detectable epitope rather than loss of membrane protection of active cargo.
dependencies: Define and source an analytically traceable exogenous intact-EV spike-in (orthogonal tracer)
Develop capture-compatibility buffer panels before interpreting capture-signal loss as membrane disruption
Ensure conditioned-medium yields sufficient for fraction-level functional testing across replicates
design_question: Daily question: Does a membrane-protected, capture-positive particle fraction recovered from MSC-conditioned medium contain the neuroinflammation-modulating bioactivity (in vitro) while matched secretome-retaining fractions do not, when assay recovery is controlled by an exogenous intact-EV spike-in?
expected_measurable_effect: Qualitative discrimination: capture-positive, spike-in-validated particle-peak fractions produce detergent/protease-sensitive reduction of LPS-induced cytokine readout in an in vitro neuroinflammation assay, whereas secretome-retaining fractions either lack this co-localizing activity or show detergent-insensitive activity.

experiment.assay: Orthogonal workflow: (1) add exogenous intact-EV spike-in to each sample prior to fractionation; (2) density/size fractionation and particle-count per fraction; (3) immuno-capture on intact fractions with separate readout for spike-in tracer and endogenous markers; (4) protease/RNase protection ± detergent on captured material (both spike-in and endogenous readouts); (5) apply fraction eluates to in vitro neuroinflammation assay and measure cytokine readouts; (6) total protein and protein:particle ratio per fraction.
experiment.comparator: Matched pair from same conditioned-medium lot: (A) bounded EV-enriched fraction spiked with exogenous intact-EV tracer versus (B) concentrated conditioned medium (secretome-retaining) spiked identically; include detergent+protease-treated aliquots and buffer-only negative controls.
experiment.control: Positive controls: characterized small EVs and dexamethasone in the bioassay. Negative controls: vehicle-only, buffer-only, and detergent-disrupted samples. Spike-in recovery serves as within-sample assay performance control.
dependencies: Availability of consistent conditioned-medium lots (same source-cell bank/passage) and sufficient yield for multi-fraction functional testing
Access to a characterized intact-EV spike-in tracer and validated capture reagents
Laboratory capability for density/size fractionation, particle counting, and in vitro neuroinflammation assays
experiment.failure_criterion: Either (A) spike-in recovery confirms assay performance but endogenous capture-positive co-localization and membrane-protected bioactivity are not reproducibly observed in bounded fractions across replicates, falsifying the hypothesis, or (B) spike-in recovery is inconsistent across replicates, preventing assay-controlled discrimination (method failure) and requiring assay redesign.
experiment.falsification_outcome: If spike-in recovery is validated but endogenous capture-positive co-localization and detergent/protease-sensitive activity do not reproducibly occur in bounded fractions, the hypothesis is falsified: the program should treat conditioned-medium-derived material as functionally indistinguishable from secretome for identity/potency decisions and redirect efforts to alternative fractionation, source-cell specification, or secretome-centric strategies.
experiment.hypothesis_tested: An orthogonal intact-EV identity gate defined by (A) recovery of an exogenous intact-EV spike-in that co-localizes with particle-count peaks and is detergent/protease-sensitive, and (B) endogenous capture-positive signal that co-localizes with particle peaks and is detergent/protease-sensitive in the bounded small-EV fraction but not in secretome-retaining concentrates, will discriminate an EV-enriched drug-substance candidate from secretome-retaining conditioned medium.
experiment.primary_readout: Presence and reproducible magnitude of anti-inflammatory effect (e.g., reduction in LPS-induced IL-6/TNF-α) that co-localizes with particle-count peaks and capture-positive fractions and is abolished by detergent + protease/RNase; plus confirmation of spike-in membrane-protected recovery in the same fractions.
experiment.question: Does a spike-in-validated, membrane-protected, capture-positive particle fraction from MSC-conditioned medium carry detergent/protease-sensitive neuroinflammation-modulating activity (in vitro) that is absent or detergent-insensitive in secretome-retaining concentrates?
required_material: MSC-conditioned medium (same source-cell lot) processed into: (A) enriched small-EV preparation (SEC/UC or program-defined bounded fraction) and (B) concentrated conditioned medium without EV enrichment (secretome-retaining), matched per lot
Exogenous characterized intact-EV spike-in (orthogonal tracer: non-overlapping species or isotope-labeled) with verified marker display
Immuno-capture reagents for canonical EV surface markers (anti-CD63/CD9/CD81 and/or TIM4/AnxA5) and capture-compatibility buffer panels
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents
Density-gradient materials (iodixanol) or SEC fractionation setup and fraction collectors
Protease (proteinase K), RNase reagents and detergent (Triton X-100 or equivalent) for membrane-disruption controls
Standardized in vitro neuroinflammation assay (e.g., LPS-stimulated human iPSC-derived microglia or primary microglia with IL-6/TNF-α ELISA or multiplex readouts)
Total protein assay reagents and consumables
Buffer-only negative controls and characterized small-EV positive control (commercial or lab-validated) processed in parallel
secondary_readouts: Spike-in recovery percentage and membrane-protection behavior per fraction
Protein:particle ratio differences between bounded fraction and secretome control
Co-localization metrics: fraction index of particle peak vs capture-positive endogenous and spike-in signals
Reproducibility across independent biological replicates (n ≥ 3 conditioned-medium lots)
experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: Across ≥3 independent conditioned-medium lots, (1) the exogenous spike-in is recovered in capture-positive, particle-peak fractions and shows loss after detergent+protease (validating assay recovery and membrane protection), and (2) endogenous capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive neuroinflammation-modulating activity are observed reproducibly in the bounded small-EV fraction but not in the secretome-retaining concentrate processed identically. This pattern enables a pass/fail identity gate (bounded fraction = EV-enriched; secretome = not EV-enriched).

explicit_inferences: Inference: Spike-in recovery controls separate assay failure from true absence of intact EV enrichment in conditioned-medium-derived materials.

Inference: A detergent/protease-sensitive functional signal that co-fractionates with capture-positive particle peaks supports EV-associated bioactivity and can serve as a candidate potency-linked identity attribute.
falsification_criteria: Spike-in recovery confirms assay performance (spike-in detected and membrane-protected) but endogenous capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks is absent in bounded fractions across independent replicates, or endogenous activity in capture-positive fractions is detergent/protease-insensitive; under these conditions the hypothesis is falsified and the material should be treated as secretome for identity/potency decisions.
human_decisions_required: Select the specific exogenous spike-in material and tracer modality (species/isotope labeling) and approve procurement
Approve the in vitro neuroinflammation assay platform and its acceptance controls
Decide whether bounded fractionation method (SEC/UC/iodixanol cushion) selected for initial experiments is the program-preferred candidate for downstream manufacturability evaluation
manufacturability_assessment: This experiment is compatible with early-stage manufacturing: bounded fractionation (e.g., SEC/iodixanol fractionation) and spike-in controls are implementable at bench scale to inform whether a manufacturable small-EV fraction is a justified drug-substance target. Yields must be sufficient to run functional assays; if not, further fractionation or concentration optimization is required.
manufacturing_rationale: Establishing an identity/potency linkage that requires a membrane-protected particle fraction enables rational fractionation gating (drug-substance definition), orthogonal QC panel selection, and early manufacturability assessments. Demonstrating spike-in recovery separates analytical failure from true absence of intact EVs, reducing downstream scale and CMC risk.
measurement_strategy: Orthogonal fraction-level analytics (particle counting, immuno-capture ELISA for intact material, spike-in tracer detection) combined with detergent + protease/RNase protection and a standardized in vitro LPS-induced cytokine readout (IL-6/TNF-α ELISA or multiplex). Include capture-compatibility buffer controls and spike-in recovery quantitation to validate assay performance.
novelty_statement: This hypothesis is novel because it combines an exogenous intact-EV spike-in recovery control with fraction-level orthogonal capture + protection analytics and a matched in vitro neuroinflammation functional assay to discriminate EV-associated activity from co-isolated soluble secretome effects. Prior program hypotheses proposed membrane-protection and capture-based signatures or functional co-fractionation alone; this proposal adds a within-sample spike-in tracer to unambiguously separate assay failure from true absence of intact-EV enrichment and couples that control directly to a discriminating bioassay.
principal_risks: Capture-reagent or buffer incompatibility may produce false-negative endogenous capture signal despite spike-in controls.
Functional assay sensitivity may be insufficient for low-biomass fractions, producing ambiguous outcomes.
Even if EV-associated activity is demonstrated in vitro, intranasal delivery and cross-species CNS exposure remain unresolved and require separate bridging studies.
proposed_potency_relationship: If a membrane-protected, capture-positive fraction reproducibly contains detergent/protease-sensitive neuroinflammation-modulating activity, then that intact-EV-associated activity can serve as a mechanism-linked, exploratory potency attribute for downstream assay development and comparability gates.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: If supported, define a candidate potency-linked product-identity attribute: a spike-in-validated, membrane-protected, capture-positive particle fraction that (A) co-localizes with particle-count peaks, (B) contains detergent/protease-sensitive neuroinflammation-modulating activity in an in vitro assay, and (C) is absent or detergent-insensitive in unpurified secretome-retaining concentrates.
title: Discriminate EV-associated versus non-EV bioactivity by matched protected-fraction functional assay (spike-in controlled)
